rationale: Iteration 0 has no race data, so this is a conservative first candidate built from the contract. Geometry: five sensors spread across the 25 mm tape at x = -0.04, -0.02, 0, 0.02, 0.04 m, all at y = 0.04 m (ahead of the axle, so the controller sees the line before the wheels reach it). Five sensors cover the tape with overlap, and 12 mm footprints keep each sensor sensitive to the line edge. Wheel track 0.12 m and radius 0.03 m give a reasonable turn-rate-to-PWM ratio. Body width 0.12 m widens the off-track limit to max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.03) = 0.06 m, which is the binding limit, so this leaves some margin. Mass 0.8 kg with a 0.18 m body length keeps yaw inertia moderate. Controller: sensor weights [-2, -1, 0, 1, 2] make the signal approximately the lateral offset in units of 0.02 m, so kp = 2.5 gives about 0.05 of wheel-speed difference per cm of error. Ki is 0 to avoid integral windup on curves. Kd = 0.05 damps oscillation without amplifying sensor noise much. Base speed 1.6 is the fastest value I judge safe on the first run; it should give roughly 1.5 m/s average. That is needed to finish within 3 s, but it may cause overshoot on tight bends. line_loss is last_direction, so the robot continues in the direction it was turning when it lost the line. Expected result: completion on the oval, with rms_error around 0.02 to 0.03 m. The slalom and s-bend may show more error at the bends. Hypotheses to test: (1) base_speed 1.6 is fast enough to finish in under 3 s without line loss; (2) kp 2.5 is stiff enough to track bends without oscillating; (3) the 0.04 m look-ahead is enough for the controller to act before the sensors leave the tape. Measurements requested: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation. These show whether speed or steering is limiting the score.
